item.text: I’m using only the earlier brief and my remembered candidate list. I’ll save distinct omissions in `followup.tsv` and won’t inspect either file afterward.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "cat > enrichment/bible/work/s103/discovery/s103-20261009/sec14/luna/followup.tsv <<'EOF'
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:1Sam.2.7	God reverses poor and rich	The commentary places noble and lowest ranks inside one human loss; Hannah's song says YHWH makes poor and rich and brings low and high down or up, making rank reversible under divine sovereignty.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:1Sam.2.8	poor raised to sit with princes	The commentary names the lowest social ranks; Hannah's song says God raises the poor from dust and seats the needy with princes, directly overturning the status scale used by Noah's accusers.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.113.7	poor lifted from dust in Hallel	The commentary recalls the lowest freedmen; this Hallel praise celebrates YHWH lifting the poor from dust and the needy from the ash heap, turning rank reversal into communal liturgy.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.113.8	needy seated with princes	The next verse says the needy are seated with princes; it gives the commentary's high/low contrast a liturgical image of the low receiving the highest social seat.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Exod.30.15	equal half-shekel for rich and poor	The census ransom is one half-shekel per person: the rich may not give more and the poor less. This Torah rule gives the commentary's inclusion of high and low a concrete equal measure.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Jer.9.22	no boasting in wisdom, might, or wealth	The commentary treats lineage and rank as human status measures; Jeremiah forbids boasting in wisdom, strength, or riches, showing that several forms of social capital cannot secure standing.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Jer.9.23	boast in knowing the God who does justice	Jeremiah redirects boasting to understanding and knowing YHWH, who practices steadfast love, justice, and righteousness; this specifies the commentary's shift from lineage to religious and ethical standing.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Zeph.3.11	haughty removed from God's mountain	The commentary says high rank cannot exempt anyone from loss; Zephaniah says God will remove the haughty from the holy mountain on the day of judgment, directly lowering status before God.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Zeph.3.12	humble remnant seeks refuge in YHWH	The commentary makes the distinction by faith and deeds; Zephaniah leaves a humble, lowly people who seek refuge in YHWH's name, joining low status to trust rather than pedigree.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.11.17	wild branches share the cultivated root	The commentary calls the root an image of lineage; Paul pictures Gentile believers grafted into Israel's olive tree to share its root, giving the lineage image a specific scene of inclusion across peoples.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.11.18	root supports branches, so do not boast	The commentary describes people grounding superiority in lineage; Paul tells the grafted branch not to boast over natural branches because the root supports it, explicitly overturning pedigree pride.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.11.20	standing by faith, not inherited branch status	The commentary says distinction turns on faith rather than lineage; Paul says natural branches were broken off through unbelief while Gentile branches stand through faith, then warns against pride.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.9.6	descent from Israel is not sufficient	The commentary denies that lineage determines the human verdict; Paul says not all descended from Israel belong to Israel, distinguishing physical descent from covenant standing.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.9.8	children of promise, not flesh alone	Paul explains that children of the flesh are not thereby God's children and that children of promise count as offspring; this gives the commentary's lineage/status issue a specific theological redefinition.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.2.28	outward identity does not decide standing	The commentary says inherited rank is not the criterion; Paul says Jewish identity and circumcision are not merely outward or bodily, challenging status carried by visible ancestry markers.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.2.29	inward identity and praise from God	Paul defines the true identity by circumcision of the heart through the Spirit and praise from God, giving the commentary's move from lineage to inward religious standing a specific formulation.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:John.1.12	believers become children of God	The commentary says lineage does not decide who belongs among the saved; John says those who receive and believe in Jesus' name are given the status of God's children.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:John.1.13	birth not from blood but from God	John specifies that God's children are not born from blood or human will but from God, directly denying natural descent as the source of religious standing.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.21.31	outcasts enter before religious leaders	In Jesus' temple dispute, he says tax collectors and prostitutes are entering God's kingdom ahead of the leaders; this closely matches the commentary's picture of elites discrediting a prophet because low-status people follow him.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.21.32	belief and repentance distinguish the groups	Jesus explains that the outcasts believed John while the leaders did not repent after seeing it; this makes response to the message, not public rank, the reason for their different standing.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Luke.18.14	tax collector justified over Pharisee	In the paired prayer scene, Jesus says the tax collector goes home justified rather than the Pharisee; the religiously prestigious figure does not outrank the despised man who humbles himself before God.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.20.26	greatness defined as service	The commentary names inherited and social rank, then says deeds mark distinction; Jesus says the one who wants to be great must become a servant, replacing status with conduct.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.20.27	first place defined as slavery to all	Jesus continues that the one who wants to be first must become a slave to all, directly reversing the rank logic behind the commentary's noble and lowest social categories.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.12.22	weaker parts are indispensable	The commentary notes that low and weak people remain within the human category; Paul says body parts that seem weaker are indispensable, giving low status a necessary role in the community.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.12.23	less honorable parts receive greater honor	Paul says the body's less honorable parts are treated with greater honor; this is a concrete reversal of rank within the community, not merely a claim that all parts exist.
strong	incil	karsi_anlati	SBLGNT:Eph.2.8	salvation as gift through faith	The commentary says the final distinction is by faith and deeds; Ephesians says salvation comes by grace through faith as God's gift, locating its source in grace and faith rather than human achievement.
strong	incil	karsi_anlati	SBLGNT:Eph.2.9	works are not the basis for boasting	Ephesians says salvation is not from works so that no one may boast, a specific difference from the commentary's formulation that righteous deeds help distinguish the saved.
medium	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Ps.8.5	Arabic ء ن س and Hebrew אנוש; table correspondence, BDB notes Arabic cognate	The commentary uses insan for the whole human species; Psalm 8 uses אנוש for the human being whom God remembers and crowns with glory and honor, a direct human-term correspondence with a strikingly dignified context.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.8.5	humanity crowned with glory and given dominion	The commentary says all humanity is in loss regardless of rank; Psalm 8 depicts the human being as remembered, crowned with glory, and given dominion, adding a distinct account of dignity bestowed by God.
medium	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Exod.16.18	Arabic خ س ر and Hebrew חסר; table sound correspondence, unverified	The commentary says high and low are included in khusr; at manna gathering, those who gather much have no surplus and those who gather little do not חסר, giving the table's unverified root match a specific scene of equal sufficiency.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Mal.2.10	one father and Creator, shared obligation	Malachi asks whether the community has one father and one Creator, then asks why its members betray one another; it connects common origin to ethical duty, while its immediate scope is covenant Israel rather than all humanity.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Acts.17.26	all nations from one ancestor	The commentary pairs lineage with the universal human category; Paul says God made every nation from one ancestor and appointed their times and boundaries, giving common human origin a concrete biblical formulation.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Acts.17.27	all peoples directed to seek God	Paul continues that the nations' situation is ordered so they might seek God; this adds a shared religious task to the common ancestry in the preceding verse.
medium	incil	karsi_anlati	SBLGNT:Eph.2.10	good works as the result of grace	The preceding verses deny that works earn salvation, but Ephesians says believers are created in Christ for good works; this preserves a role for deeds while locating them as the result, not the basis, of salvation.
medium	tevrat	soydas	Sanhedrin 37a	Adam's seal and each person's uniqueness	The Mishnah's single Adam is expanded: humanity bears one divine seal, yet no person resembles another and each must regard the world as created for them. This adds individual worth to the commentary's inclusion of every rank.
medium	incil	yorum_gelenegi	1 Clement 13:1	Christian reception of Jeremiah's anti-boasting formula	Clement applies Jeremiah's warning against boasting in wisdom, strength, and wealth to Christian humility, giving an early Christian interpretation of the status critique in Jeremiah 9.
medium	incil	motif	Didache 4:3	impartial correction and just judgment	The church rule commands just judgment and no partiality when correcting transgressions; it gives the commentary's move from rank to religious conduct a concrete communal practice.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.12.16	associate with the lowly, do not be haughty	Paul tells the community not to be proud and to associate with the lowly; the Greek can also mean associating with humble things, so this is a specific but textually ambiguous answer to elite distance from low-status people.
EOF"

Accuracy notes: the listed Hebrew/Aramaic sound matches are marked unverified, and the Romans 12:16 proposal flags its translation ambiguity.
